strings.name: Amartya Sen
strings.summary: Amartya Sen connects economics with ethics through research on collective choice, poverty, famine and people’s real opportunities. His capability approach asks what people can do and become, extending evaluation beyond income alone. His scholarship and public writing shaped welfare economics, development policy and debates on justice; he received the economics Nobel in 1998.
strings.coverageNote: Sources checked through 13 November 2026. The timeline emphasizes scholarship and major books, ending with the 2021 memoir. Current Harvard information was checked; former appointments are not presented as current.
strings.influence.rationale: Reshaped public discussion of development and poverty through welfare economics, the capability approach and research on famine.

strings.highlights.highlight-1.title: Welfare and social choice
strings.highlights.highlight-1.text: Studied how personal interests and rights inform social evaluation; received the 1998 economics Nobel.
strings.highlights.highlight-2.title: Development and capabilities
strings.highlights.highlight-2.text: Linked poverty, famine and development to effective freedoms, education and health.
strings.timeline.event-1.title: Memoir published
strings.timeline.event-1.text: Home in the World recalled his upbringing in India and international academic life.
strings.timeline.event-2.title: The Idea of Justice
strings.timeline.event-2.text: Examined justice and public reasoning through comparisons of real injustices.
strings.timeline.event-3.title: Development as Freedom
strings.timeline.event-3.text: Explained development as an expansion of substantive human freedoms.
strings.timeline.event-4.title: Economics Nobel
strings.timeline.event-4.text: Recognized for welfare economics; also began serving as Master of Trinity College, Cambridge.
strings.timeline.event-5.title: Joins Harvard
strings.timeline.event-5.text: Became a professor of economics and philosophy, continuing interdisciplinary research.
strings.timeline.event-6.title: Poverty and Famines
strings.timeline.event-6.text: Examined access and entitlements to food rather than food supply alone.
strings.timeline.event-7.title: Social-choice monograph
strings.timeline.event-7.text: Published Collective Choice and Social Welfare, advancing social-choice theory.
strings.timeline.event-8.title: Cambridge doctorate
strings.timeline.event-8.text: Completed doctoral study after studying economics in Calcutta and Cambridge; later taught internationally.
strings.timeline.event-9.title: Born in Santiniketan
strings.timeline.event-9.text: Grew up in Bengal; early experiences informed his concern with famine and inequality.
